sw-001.label: Connects your code to a Foundry project using an endpoint and credential (package azure-ai-projects)
sw-001.why: AIProjectClient(endpoint, credential) is the project entry point; get_openai_client() hangs off it — remove auth and this is the line that breaks.

sw-002.label: Sends the messages list to a deployed model and returns choices[0].message.content
sw-002.why: chat.completions.create(model=DEPLOYMENT_NAME, messages=[…]) is the chat call — and model= takes the deployment name, not the base model name (histack trap #5).

sw-003.label: Holds your Speech resource key and region, and the synthesis voice name
sw-003.why: SpeechConfig(key, region) is configured first (e.g. speech_synthesis_voice_name='en-US-Ava:DragonHDLatestNeural'); AudioConfig handles devices, not credentials.

sw-004.label: Send the user's spoken question as inline audio data inside the message content
sw-004.why: Spoken INPUT goes in message content parts as input_audio; the response-settings twin is the documented trap.

sw-005.label: Ask the model to answer with spoken audio: voice "alloy", format "wav"
sw-005.why: Spoken OUTPUT is requested via modalities=["text","audio"] plus audio={"voice":"alloy","format":"wav"} on the multimodal call — the exam's exact payload.

sw-006.label: Include a photo (URL or base64) in a chat message so the deployed gpt-4o can describe it
sw-006.why: Visual input travels as image_url / base64 content parts to a multimodal deployment — not through the Vision SDK, which is a different service and endpoint (pair #23).

sw-007.label: Bridges an existing project client to the OpenAI-compatible client used for Responses and Conversations calls
sw-007.why: project.get_openai_client() is an instance method called on the project object; the exam's trap is calling it on the class itself instead.

sw-008.label: Called once, right after the project client is built, before the first Responses or Conversations request goes out
sw-008.why: It is the runtime bridge that hands back the OpenAI-shaped client; the credential object only authenticates the project client, it never returns a chat client.

sw-009.label: Passed with zero arguments as the credential= value so the app authenticates via signed-in Azure identity, no key typed anywhere
sw-009.why: DefaultAzureCredential() is the keyless Entra ID credential object; AIProjectClient is what consumes it, and azure-ai-projects is only the package name, not a runtime object.

sw-010.label: The object az login sets up for: the client resolves your signed-in identity from it automatically at call time, no environment API key needed
sw-010.why: The quickstart pairs az login with this credential object; get_openai_client only returns a chat client and has nothing to do with authentication.

sw-011.label: The pip package you install before writing any Foundry project client code, per the quickstart's very first setup command
sw-011.why: "Which package should you install for the project client?" is a classic exam stem — the answer is azure-ai-projects, not the search or language SDKs.

sw-012.label: Listed alongside az login in the quickstart setup steps, pinned to a minimum version (>=2.0.0) before any client code runs
sw-012.why: The documented quickstart guidance installs azure-ai-projects>=2.0.0 and runs az login — the Vision and Search packages are unrelated to the project client.

sw-013.label: Constructed with an endpoint and an AzureKeyCredential before any key-phrase or sentiment call can run against plain text
sw-013.why: TextAnalyticsClient(endpoint, credential) exposes.extract_key_phrases()/.analyze_sentiment() on raw text; the other two clients target multimodal documents and images at different endpoints entirely.

sw-014.label: Whichever client type exposes analyze_sentiment(documents) so each document's overall sentiment gets printed back
sw-014.why: Sentiment and key-phrase extraction are AI Language text-analytics methods on this client; the other two operate on multimodal documents or live audio, not plain text.

sw-015.label: Set to listen from the computer's default microphone instead of a saved file, then handed to the recognizer as its audio source
sw-015.why: AudioConfig(use_default_microphone=True) picks the input device; SpeechConfig instead holds the subscription key/region, and SpeechRecognizer is the class this object gets passed into, not the device selector itself.

sw-016.label: Built from a saved filename so a recognizer reads speech from a test WAV file instead of a live microphone
sw-016.why: AudioConfig(filename=…) is the file-backed device source; SpeechConfig carries credentials and voice name, and SpeechSynthesizer plays audio out rather than reading it in.

sw-017.label: Given both a speech config and an audio config, then called to capture exactly one short spoken utterance and stop
sw-017.why: This is the class whose recognize_once_async() captures a single utterance; SpeechSynthesizer instead speaks text out, and AudioConfig only wires up the input device.

sw-018.label: Its single-utterance async call returns a result object whose.text holds the transcript of what the microphone just heard
sw-018.why: The speech-to-text class returns result.text from recognizing live audio; the synthesizer speaks instead of listens, and the Language client only ever works on text that's already been transcribed.

sw-019.label: Takes a speech config with the voice name already set, then turns a text string into spoken output through the speaker
sw-019.why: This class's speak_text_async() plays a string aloud using the configured voice; the recognizer instead converts speech to text, and AudioConfig only selects a device.

sw-020.label: After a recognizer produces a text transcript, this second object reads that same string back out loud with its own async speak call
sw-020.why: Text-to-speech playback of the recognized reply is this class's job; the recognizer already produced the text, and SpeechConfig only stores credentials and the voice name it uses.

sw-021.label: Constructed with an endpoint and key, then its single call analyzes an image URL for the READ visual feature to pull text off a photo
sw-021.why: This Vision client's.analyze(image_url=…, visual_features=[…]) call runs OCR on general images; ContentUnderstandingClient instead returns a poller from a very different, asynchronous call shape.

sw-022.label: Its captioning-plus-OCR call takes the image by URL rather than raw bytes, requesting both CAPTION and READ features in one pass
sw-022.why: This Vision client's by-URL analysis method returns fixed prebuilt features like caption and read; it has no polling step and no relation to speech capture at all.

sw-023.label: The client an app creates first when it will send document URLs off for extraction and read structured results back
sw-023.why: "Which client should the app create first?" for a Content Understanding app is this class — the other two are separate services with separate endpoints for plain text and general images respectively.

sw-024.label: Its long-running analyze call returns a poller; calling.result() on that poller is how the app waits for the final extracted output
sw-024.why: begin_analyze() plus poller.result() is this client's asynchronous polling pattern; the Vision client's analyze() is synchronous, and the Language client's methods take documents directly with no polling.

sw-025.label: The image-generation request whose response field b64_json holds the actual pixel data you decode, not a url field
sw-025.why: A GPT-image-1 deployment returns generated image bytes in response.data[0].b64_json; a completions call returns text choices, and the Vision client only analyzes an image that already exists.

sw-026.label: Set background to transparent and request PNG output on this text-to-image request to get a see-through background
sw-026.why: Transparent background plus PNG output are GPT-image-1-series generation parameters; nothing in the Vision analysis or chat-completion calls accepts them.
